subject: Post-call: buying map & contract pathway for Acme Health pilot
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: buying map & contract pathway for Acme Health pilot

Alex — great conversation this morning, thanks for taking the time. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with your procurement/legal cadence.

Summary of call:
- Use case: Proof-of-concept (pilot) to evaluate Redwood inference for clinical notes summarization (de-id pipeline).
- Key success criteria: sub-100ms median latency at 8k tokens/session, 95% reduction in manual triage time, demonstrable privacy controls (KMS + VPC).

Stakeholder map I captured (please correct/add):
- Economic buyer: Priya Shah (VP, Product) — final sign-off on budget.
- Technical champion: Alex Turner (Dir. Data Eng) — owns pilot delivery.
- Security/compliance: Priya also loops legal/security; she said legal will want the security questionnaire completed prior to broad data exchange.
- Procurement/ops: unknown contact; likely shared PO process after MSA.

Suggested contract routing (our recommended path to minimize blockers):
1) NDA (one-way or mutual) — quick, enables exchange of sample data and SSO details.
2) Security questionnaire (Acme->Redwood) + SSO/KMS diagram exchange.
3) DPA (if needed for pilot) and SOW for pilot scope and success criteria.
4) MSA + commercial terms (concurrent with SOW redlines).

Estimated turn times (please confirm with your teams):
- NDA: 2–4 business days (typical)
- Security questionnaire: 3–7 business days to complete communications
- MSA redlines: 7–15 business days depending on negotiation scope
- Procurement PO after MSA: 2–4 weeks

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm the procurement contact and whether they require a PO before starting the pilot?
- Will legal accept a Redwood standard NDA via DocuSign, or do you prefer to circulate Acme's form (if so, please share)?
- I'll loop Rishi (contracts) and Ben (AE) on the next exchange so redlines can be handled quickly.

Attachments I can provide now: Redwood standard NDA (attached), Redwood pilot SOW template, sample security questionnaire.

Thanks — I’ll hold off on sending any formal documents until I hear your preference on the NDA.

—
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | (415) 555-0189

Naomi — thanks for the write-up, looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side:

Stakeholders (confirmed):
- Economic buyer: Priya Shah (VP, Product) — copied.
- Procurement: Brian Lowe (Procurement Manager) — brian.lowe@acmehealth.com (I’ll loop him if we move to commercial).
- Legal: Priya will introduce our legal lead if we need to swap formal contracts. For NDA we can accept your standard mutual NDA via DocuSign (preferred).

Timing:
- NDA: we usually turn around mutual NDAs in 48–72 hours if it’s our preferred template; if we circulate our form, it can take longer. Please send your DocuSign and we’ll review.
- Security questionnaire: Priya flagged that our security team will want to see KMS/HSM details and data-at-rest diagrams — they aim for 5 business days to review once they have the initial answers.
- MSA: our legal tends to take up to 2 weeks to redline initial MSA drafts; procurement PO typically follows the legal/finance signoff (3–4 weeks).

I’m attaching our preliminary security questionnaire and a contact for Brian in procurement.

Regards,
Alex Turner
Director, Data Engineering
Acme Health
alex.turner@acmehealth.com

- Procurement contact (Brian Lowe) added — expectation: if we proceed beyond pilot, PO required; flag for revenue ops.
- Rishi: can you estimate fallback SLA for redline turnaround? We should push for a 5–7 business day target on NDA and 7–10 for initial MSA redlines to keep momentum.

Internal action items:
- Rishi: draft NDA + cover note by end of day tomorrow.
- Marissa: I’ll prep a commercial kicker if we need to offer pilot credits to accelerate sign-off.

Subject: Next steps & proposed timeline for NDA -> pilot kickoff

Alex / Brian / Priya — looping Brian to bring procurement visibility. Based on your preferences we propose this sequence:

1) Naomi -> sends mutual NDA via DocuSign (today).
2) Acme legal review (target 2–3 business days).
3) Security questionnaire exchange (we’ll fill Redwood answers and return; target 5 business days).
4) Sign NDA -> exchange sample dataset (masked) and schedule technical kickoff within 3 business days of NDA signature.
5) Concurrent: Redwood to provide SOW + proposed pilot budget; Acme procurement to indicate PO cadence if pilot converts.

Action items:
- Ben: attach Redwood NDA and DocuSign link when ready.
- Priya: confirm security reviewer point-of-contact for the questionnaire.
- Brian: please confirm whether Acme requires a purchase order before pilot start or only after MSA sign-off.

We’ll aim to keep legal redlines minimal — propose we handle technical/security scoping in the SOW and reserve heavier commercial negotiation for MSA stage.

Attachments: Acme_NDA_v1.pdf (Redwood standard mutual NDA), Redwood_MSA_template.docx (reference).

Thanks,
Naomi

Naomi / team — quick confirmation from Acme legal/procurement side:

- We accept Redwood’s mutual NDA via DocuSign. Our legal team (Priya Shah) usually turns NDA reviews around in 2–3 business days.
- Security review: our InfoSec lead (Samir Patel, samir.patel@acmehealth.com) will take roughly 5 business days to review the questionnaire and KMS diagram once received.

- Procurement: Brian confirms we do NOT require a PO for an initial pilot (we can proceed with a limited-scope SOW and demo). If pilot converts to paid production, procurement will require a PO (3–4 week cadence).
